guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the every-other-combat Power card reward option is entirely missing, and it is the game's ONLY implementation of the EARLY TryModifyCardRewardOptions pass
guards.issue: MECHANISM: LastingCandy.cs:114-135 takes `creationOptions.GetPossibleCards(player)`, keeps the Power-type cards not already offered (falling back to all Power cards if that set is empty), builds a fresh CardCreationOptions with source Other and flags NoModifyHooks | NoCardPoolModifications, runs `CardFactory.CreateForReward(Owner, 1, options2)` and APPENDS the result to the options list. lasting_candy.py implements nothing. PREMISE CHECK (PROMPT.md bug class 12): the docstring says 'a card-reward modifier that runs between combats, so this is a no-op stub' -- false. `Relic.modify_card_reward_options` exists (relics/base.py:172-176) and rewards.py:299-301 dispatches it over run.relics inside create_reward_cards; the shared sweep-stub-premises already reports this pipeline as live. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py tools/audit/relic_probes_b08.py b08-candy): Lasting Candy is Uncommon in the transcribed grab bag (b08-pool), and a MONSTER card reward on the second combat of a run comes out as the same three cards ['battle_trance', 'twin_strike', 'expect_a_fight'] with and without the relic, where the game adds a fourth, always-Power option. The same probe's b08-lavalamp run shows relic/silver_crucible mutating reward options through that very hook today, so the sim demonstrably can do this. SECOND OBSERVABLE: the added card costs a rarity roll, an item pick and an upgrade roll on the per-player Rewards stream (CardFactory.cs:214-241 and RollForUpgrade at CardFactory.cs, reached because options2 carries no NoUpgradeRoll flag), none of which the sim consumes -- so every later Rewards draw in the run is shifted for the conformance harness. Rule 7: relics/base.py, rewards.py, relics/silver_crucible.py and src/Core/Factories/CardFactory.cs are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: G2 (LIVE): LastingCandy is the SEVENTEENTH member of the `IsBeforeAct3TreasureChest` (TotalFloor < 41) cluster, not a separate 'unlock gate' unit -- correcting .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md sweep B
guards.issue: MECHANISM: LastingCandy.cs:97 ends `return RelicModel.IsBeforeAct3TreasureChest(runState);`, which is `TotalFloor < 41` in single-player (RelicModel.cs:452-456). RelicGrabBag.RemoveDisallowedRelicsFromDeques (RelicGrabBag.cs:250-271) permanently REMOVES every relic whose IsAllowed is false from the rarity deques, so from floor 41 the game stops offering it and every subsequent pull shifts. `sts2_rl.relics.base.Relic` declares no is_allowed member (EXECUTED: `hasattr(Relic, 'is_allowed')` is False) and pull_relic_from_front applies no such filter. SWEEP CORRECTION: sweep B bucket (a) lists SIXTEEN relics and files this one separately in bucket (c) as 'gated on the Ironclad's UnlockState ... likely a waiver, but it needs the per-unit audit'. The reason is mechanical: the sweep's regex captures only the FIRST statement of an IsAllowed body, and Lasting Candy is the pool's ONLY multi-clause body. `py tools/audit/relic_probes_b08.py b08-isallowed` brace-matches every body instead and prints 17 relics containing IsBeforeAct3TreasureChest, with lasting_candy flagged MULTI-CLAUSE and the other 16 all bare `return` statements; the remaining three overrides are the single-player-constant player-count gates. So the single-fix cluster sweep B sizes is 17, and the answer to its open question is: NOT a waiver -- this relic carries the same LIVE pool-composition gap as amethyst_aubergine. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed): at total_floor=60 a bag containing lasting_candy still yields it, and RunState already tracks total_floor, so the predicate is expressible today. Same mechanism, same verdict as audits/relic/amethyst_aubergine.json's IsAllowed entry (binding rule 3). Rule 7: src/Core/Models/RelicModel.cs, src/Core/Runs/RelicGrabBag.cs, relics/base.py and run.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: G3 (DORMANT): the FIRST clause -- `runState.Players.Any(p => p.Character is Ironclad && p.UnlockState.NumberOfRuns == 0)` vetoes the relic on a profile's very first Ironclad run
guards.issue: MECHANISM: LastingCandy.cs:82-96. The sim has no profile/unlock model at all -- `grep -rn 'UnlockState\|NumberOfRuns' sts2_rl/` returns nothing and RunState has no notion of how many runs the profile has played -- so the sim behaves as a veteran profile always. RECORDED AS A DORMANT GAP, NOT A WAIVER, per binding rule 1: 'the sim has no such system' is explicitly a dormant gap, and unlocks are not one of the contract's four waiver categories (multiplayer, presentation, ascension, other characters). This is the answer sweep B left open ('likely a waiver, but this batch must say so with a reason') -- the reason it is not a waiver is rule 1, and the reason it is dormant rather than live is that the concrete unported thing is a per-profile UnlockState with NumberOfRuns; the conformance seeds all come from a profile with many completed runs, so the clause evaluates false there and the sim's behaviour coincides. It also cannot be the whole story about this relic's IsAllowed -- see G2. The Ironclad-character half of the predicate is inside the shared contract's Ironclad-only scope and needs no waiver.

guards.what: G4 (DORMANT): the sim's single `modify_card_reward_options` collapses C#'s EARLY and LATE card-reward passes, and Lasting Candy is the only early implementer
guards.issue: MECHANISM: Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions (Hook.cs:1445-1467) runs every listener's TryModifyCardRewardOptions in a FIRST full pass, then every listener's TryModifyCardRewardOptionsLate in a SECOND. rewards.py:299-301 is one flat loop, and the sim's `Relic.modify_card_reward_options` docstring (relics/base.py:172-176) names it TryModifyCardRewardOptionsLate. A census of the game source finds Lasting Candy is the ONLY non-mock override of the early pass and nine relics override the Late one (fresnel_lens, frozen_egg, glitter, lava_lamp, molten_egg, silken_tress, silver_crucible, toxic_egg, wing_charm). The phase order is load-bearing precisely for this relic: the added Power option must exist BEFORE Glitter enchants, Silver Crucible upgrades or the eggs upgrade the option list, otherwise the fourth option is left un-enchanted and un-upgraded. DORMANT TODAY only because G1 leaves the early pass empty -- so the flat loop cannot mis-order anything. FIX-ORDERING CONSTRAINT, which is why this is filed separately: fixing G1 inside the existing flat loop introduces the mis-ordering, so the phase split must land with it. The ported Late implementers (relics/glitter.py:16, relics/silver_crucible.py:28, relics/silken_tress.py:27, relics/_eggs.py:39) are all already in the same loop. Rule 7: src/Core/Hooks/Hook.cs, rewards.py, relics/base.py, relics/glitter.py, relics/silver_crucible.py, relics/silken_tress.py and relics/_eggs.py are not hashed by this record.
